title: add-ci-artifact-signing-provenance-and-release-manifests-for-private-installer
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Add end-to-end CI for Private Installer release artifacts: generate SBOMs (syft), produce signed provenance JSON, cosign-sign container artifacts and release manifests, and publish release manifests to S3. Enables verifiable on-prem releases for compliance-sensitive customers.
description: Motivation: Private Installer releases are consumed by regulated customers that require verifiable provenance and signed artifacts. This PR wires up CI steps to produce SBOMs, provenance metadata, and cosign signatures for container images and release manifests so customers can validate release integrity. Scope: - Add a GitHub Actions workflow (installer/.github/workflows/publish-release-manifests.yml) that runs on tag and on manual dispatch. - Generate SBOMs using Syft for all release images and include them in the release bundle. - Produce a provenance JSON (in the format used by our release automation) that includes build info, SBOM references, and cosign signatures. - Run cosign to sign images and manifest blobs; support both KMS-backed ephemeral keys (CI) and customer-provided keys (docs). - Publish signed release-manifests.tar.gz to the release bucket with provenance metadata and SHA256 checksums. - Small Helm chart tweaks to include manifest references for offline install workflows. Checklist: - [x] CI workflow added - [x] SBOM generation with syft - [x] Provenance manifest generation - [x] cosign signing step + pinned cosign version - [x] Publish to S3 with checksum - [x] Docs section for key rotation and verification - [x] Tests: integration job that verifies signatures via cosign verify Notes: This PR is intentionally conservative about changing installer code; most changes are CI/infra and release packaging. See commits for details.
commits_summary: 5 commits: initial workflow and scripts; add syft SBOM generation and parsing; provenance JSON builder; cosign integration and key handling; Helm manifest reference updates and docs. Each commit is focused and includes small test vectors used by CI integration job.
review_comments: Evan Brown: Overall looks good — can we pin the cosign version to avoid CI drift? Also please add tests that exercise keyless verification in the integration job.
Maya Chen: Pinning cosign to 2.1.0 (matches infra images). Added an integration step that verifies signatures using cosign verify with the same key used by CI (ephemeral KMS-backed key).
Priya Nair: Minor nit: document how customers provide their cosign key and how rotation works. Also ensure SBOMs include image digest not tag.
Maya Chen: Added docs/private-installer/release-verification.md with key rotation guidance and verification commands. Updated SBOM generation to record image digest produced by the build pipeline.
Luca Moretti: CI failed initially due to ephemeral key permissions on staging KMS. Can you add a retry and clearer error for missing permissions?
Maya Chen: Added retry logic to cosign_sign.sh and explicit permission check with a helpful error message. Reran CI and all checks passed.
ci_checks: GitHub Actions: integration (initial fail, rerun pass)
notes_for_ops: The workflow requires the following secrets and permissions in the repo: RELEASE_S3_BUCKET, COSIGN_KMS_KEY (for CI ephemeral keys), COSIGN_PASSWORD (if using static key fallback), AWS_CREDENTIALS with putObject rights. A runbook section was added to docs/private-installer/release-verification.md explaining verification and key rotation.
testing_notes: Integration job uses a small test image published to the staging registry. CI verifies SBOM existence, checks that SBOM references image digest, verifies cosign signatures (cosign verify), and checks that provenance JSON contains expected fields (builder, build_time, sbom_refs, signatures).
backports: No backports required — workflow runs on tag events only. For older long-lived branches we will add a follow-up if requested by SRE.
